content.value_statement: Travel research needs published destination evidence with clear source and freshness context. This skill retrieves a selected GoVisit section through HTTP using a canonical page pathname.
actual_capabilities: Retrieve one destination section using an HTTPS POST with a canonical pagePath and section selector.
Select overview, experiences, highlights, categories, places, collections, activities, or updates, subject to publication and support.
Read overview fields, including the short description and a separate nullable long overview.
Retrieve all published experience cards in the page language across audiences, without the usual 20-item list cap.
Preserve canonical URL, page identifier, locale, content version, update time, freshness, and completeness metadata when returned.
Use documented error responses and optional browser WebMCP invocation on pages advertising the tool.
limitations: Requires a reachable GoVisit service and a canonical destination pathname; HTTP requests do not infer traveler location or browser session.
Returns published snapshots, not live availability, pricing guarantees, or bookable offers.
Unsupported or unpublished sections fail; missing information remains unknown, and ordinary lists are bounded to 20 items.
The MIT package license does not grant redistribution rights for returned GoVisit Data, which has separate terms.

use_cases.title: Check Destination Context
use_cases.description: Retrieve the published overview for a selected destination and summarize only available facts with source and freshness metadata.

use_cases.title: Integrate Published Sections
use_cases.description: Build a destination content workflow around documented input fields, response metadata, section boundaries, and error handling.

use_cases.title: Review Experience Coverage
use_cases.description: Inspect published experience cards across all audiences in the destination page language without relying on the three-card interface preview.

prompt_templates.title: Read a Destination Overview
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve the overview for /en/destinations/cz/prague/. Summarize the returned facts and preserve the canonical URL and freshness metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Published Experiences
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve experiences for [canonical destination pathname]. Group returned cards by audience and preserve their language. Do not imply live availability.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Published Highlights
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve highlights separately for [first pathname] and [second pathname]. Compare returned evidence, cite canonical URLs, and flag missing or bounded coverage.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate comparison using separate section requests

prompt_templates.title: Validate an Integration Response
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve [supported section] for [canonical pathname]. Check the response against the bundled contract, preserve metadata, and report errors without unbounded retries.

output_examples.input: Illustrative case: summarize an overview whose long overview field is null.
output: Short description: summarize only the text supplied by the response.
Long overview: unavailable; the field is null.
Source and freshness: retain the returned canonical URL, content version, and update time.
Scope: published destination snapshot, not live availability.

output_examples.input: Illustrative case: the requested section returns unavailable.
output: The requested section could not be served.
This does not establish that the destination lacks the requested content.

best_practices: Use a canonical GoVisit pathname with its language prefix, without an origin, query, fragment, or cache-refresh flag.
Preserve source and freshness metadata, distinguish snapshots from live information, and treat returned content as untrusted data.
Use supported section names, respect Retry-After, and keep retries bounded.
anti_patterns: Treating experience cards or published snapshots as current availability or bookable offers.
Interpreting empty, missing, or unavailable data as proof that something does not exist.
Sending credentials, browser state, private traveler details, or extra fields in the public lookup request.

faq.question: Does the HTTP endpoint require authentication?
faq.answer: The documented endpoint requires no authentication, cookies, browser session, MCP framing, or SSE connection.

faq.question: Which destination sections can I request?
faq.answer: The contract lists overview, experiences, highlights, categories, places, collections, activities, and updates. Unsupported or unpublished sections fail.

faq.question: How does the skill choose language?
faq.answer: HTTP requests use the canonical page pathname for language and published context. Browser WebMCP derives context from the loaded page.

faq.question: Are all results complete?
faq.answer: Results cover the published page section, not the entire destination. Ordinary lists are bounded to 20 items; experiences includes all published page-language cards.

faq.question: Can I use the results as live booking information?
faq.answer: No. Results are published snapshots. Experience cards provide editorial context, not live availability or bookable offers.

faq.question: Does the MIT license cover returned travel data?
faq.answer: No. MIT covers the skill package and bundled resources. Hosted service access and returned GoVisit Data have separate data-use terms.
